title: Rollout: a new session host image breaks the claims app on every new host

brief.situation: You are the AVD administrator at Merrow Insurance. Session hosts for hp-claims are built from the Compute Gallery image definition win11-claims, referenced as 'latest'. Last night image version 2.4.0 (monthly updates plus a new PDF component) was published. Six hosts were added at 07:00 from it; on those, the claims app crashes when it opens a PDF. Autoscale adds ten more hosts at 10:00 for the second shift.
handover: The previous version, 2.3.0, has run for a month without problems.
24 agents are working on the six new hosts right now; each holds open claims.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the gallery's image versions, what 'latest' resolves to and which hosts were built from which.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why only some hosts crashed, how you stopped the spread, and how the next image is gated.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects crashes to one image version.
parts.modelAnswer: Only claims-34..39 crash, all built at 07:00 from 2.4.0; the crash is in the PDF component new in that version. The host pool builds from 'latest', which resolved to 2.4.0.

parts.label: Spread
parts.criteria: Makes latest safe, then moves users gently.
parts.modelAnswer: Set excludeFromLatest on 2.4.0 so the 10:00 scale-out uses 2.3.0; drained the six hosts and asked their users to save and reconnect. Deleting them would have lost open claims and rebuilt from the same image.

parts.label: Gate
parts.modelAnswer: The six are replaced from 2.3.0 when empty; new versions publish excluded from latest until a canary passes a PDF smoke test.

expertPath.text: Crashing hosts all 2.4.0; latest = 2.4.0; crash in pdfrender64.dll; 24 users on them.
excludeFromLatest on 2.4.0; drain and message; replace when empty; pipeline gate.
latest = 2.3.0; PDF opens on a 2.3.0 host.

workLost.headline: Stop the spread before you remove the symptom
workLost.body: First make 'latest' safe (exclude the bad version), then drain the bad hosts and replace them when they empty. Deleting hosts with users on them loses work, and rebuilds from 'latest' bring the problem back.

spread.headline: 'latest' kept pointing at the broken version
spread.body: A host pool that builds from 'latest' takes whatever is newest. Exclude a bad version from latest (or pin a known-good version) before the next scale-out.

contained.headline: Good: image lifecycle as a control
contained.body: You tied the crash to one image version, made 'latest' safe before the scale-out, moved users off without logging them out, checked, and put a test gate in the image pipeline.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Only the hosts built from image 2.4.0 crash, and the host pool builds from 'latest', which is 2.4.0, so the 10:00 scale-out would spread it. Exclude 2.4.0 from latest so new hosts use 2.3.0, drain the six broken hosts and ask their users to save and reconnect, then replace them when empty and gate future versions behind a canary test. Deleting hosts with users on them loses work and rebuilds from the same image; restarts change nothing.
